bossChallenges.scenario: A glowing treasure chest just dropped in Monster Mountain! Each team must open a loot box and describe what the monster inside is wearing before the timer runs out.
bossChallenges.game: Loot Box Relay: teams take turns opening a drawn clothing card, saying 'I like the ___' or 'I don't like the ___', and matching it to the right monster on the whiteboard.
bossChallenges.winCondition: First team to correctly describe 5 loot items wins the chest.

bossChallenges.scenario: It's Superhero Costume Day! Every hero's closet got mixed up and the team must sort the pile before the villain arrives.
bossChallenges.game: Closet Sort: students race to place clothing cards under 'I like' or 'I don't like' while saying the full sentence out loud.
bossChallenges.winCondition: First team to sort and say all 6 items correctly saves the city.

bossChallenges.scenario: The Jungle Animal Fashion Show is starting and the runway needs an announcer team for each animal model!
bossChallenges.game: Runway Roleplay: one student models a clothing card while their teammate announces 'He/She is wearing a ___' to the judges.
bossChallenges.winCondition: The team with the loudest, clearest announcement for all their models wins Best Show.

hooks: Quick warm-up: a giant laundry basket of clothing pictures spills onto the board — students race to name each item in English before the buzzer.
Play 'Monster Dress-Up': the teacher draws a silly monster and students shout clothing words to dress it, one item at a time.
discoveries: Draw a friendly monster on the board wearing five different clothing items. Point to each and model 'I like the ___' / 'I don't like the ___', then have students echo with their own true opinion.
Introduce a magic wardrobe that only opens for correct sentences — students must say 'I like...' or 'I don't like...' about a revealed item to see what's inside.
conceptChecks: If I say 'I don't like the hat,' am I happy or unhappy about the hat?
Which word changes the sentence from happy to unhappy — 'like' or 'don't like'?
Point to the monster wearing the jacket it LIKES.
sandboxActivities: In pairs, students take turns flipping clothing cards and saying 'I like the ___' or 'I don't like the ___' for each one.
Students draw their own monster on paper and label three things it likes wearing and one thing it doesn't.

ruleRecaps: Remember: 'I like' + a clothing word for things we enjoy, 'I don't like' + a clothing word for things we don't. Blue boxes = the subject (I, she, he), Red boxes = the verb (like/don't like).
Quick recap on the board: 'She likes the dress.' vs 'She doesn't like the dress.' — same clothing word, opposite feeling.
matchingActivities: Drag-and-drop: match each clothing emoji card to the correct 'likes' or 'doesn't like' speech bubble on the board.
Students match a clothing word card to a weather icon (warm vs. cool) and say a full sentence about it.
bossTasks: Each student picks one real item they're wearing today and says one full sentence about whether they like it.
Students interview a partner: 'Do you like ___?' and report the answer back to the class in a full sentence.

bossChallenges.scenario: The Battle Royale wardrobe just dropped a legendary crate! Teams must call out what's inside before the storm closes in.
bossChallenges.game: Loot Crate Showdown: a card is revealed and one player must say 'I like the ___' or 'I don't like the ___' before their teammate confirms it's correct.
bossChallenges.winCondition: First team to correctly call 5 crate drops wins the match.

bossChallenges.scenario: A streamer is doing a live 'Rate My Fit' check and needs real-time chat comments in English.
bossChallenges.game: Rate My Fit: one student models an outfit card while teammates type/say chat-style comments like 'I like the drip on that hoodie 🔥'.
bossChallenges.winCondition: The team with the most complete, grammatically correct comments wins the stream.

bossChallenges.scenario: It's the last day before a big trip and the group chat is arguing about what to pack.
bossChallenges.game: Group Chat Debate: teams must agree on 5 items to pack, justifying each with 'I like...' / 'I don't like...' sentences.
bossChallenges.winCondition: The team that reaches full agreement first, using correct sentences, wins.

hooks: Quick warm-up: flash outfit photos on the board and students shout the item name in English before the next one appears.
Play 'Fit Check': the teacher describes a mystery outfit one item at a time and students guess who's wearing it.
discoveries: Show a streamer's 'fit check' clip idea on the board with five outfit items. Model 'I like the ___' / 'I don't like the ___' for each, then have students give their own real opinion.
Introduce a 'loot crate' that only opens for a correct sentence — students say 'I like...' or 'I don't like...' about a revealed item to unlock it.
conceptChecks: If I say 'I don't like the cap,' does that mean I want to wear it?
Which word flips the sentence's meaning — 'like' or 'don't like'?
Point to the outfit the streamer says they like.
sandboxActivities: In pairs, students flip outfit cards and take turns saying 'I like the ___' or 'I don't like the ___.'
Students sketch their own 'dream fit' and label three pieces they like and one they don't.

ruleRecaps: Recap: 'I like' + item for things we're into, 'I don't like' + item for things we're not. Blue = the subject (I, she, he), Red = the verb (like/don't like).
Board recap: 'She likes the hoodie.' vs 'She doesn't like the hoodie.' — same item, opposite opinion.
matchingActivities: Drag-and-drop: match each outfit emoji to the correct 'likes' or 'doesn't like' chat bubble.
Students match an item card to a vibe word (fire vs. drip) and say a full sentence about it.
bossTasks: Each student picks one real item they're wearing today and gives a full sentence opinion on it.
Students interview a partner: 'Do you like ___?' and report the answer back in a full sentence.

bossChallenges.scenario: Enrollment Day at Titan Academy! Every new hero must introduce themselves to the Headmaster before earning their cape.
bossChallenges.game: Hero Roll Call: each student steps up and says 'Hello, I am ___!' plus one color and number about their gear before the buzzer.
bossChallenges.winCondition: First team where every hero introduces themselves correctly wins their capes.

bossChallenges.scenario: The Academy's Color Alarm just went off — capes are missing colors and only correct sentences will restore them!
bossChallenges.game: Cape Repair Relay: a student draws a color card and must say 'My cape is ___' to fix it, then the next teammate goes.
bossChallenges.winCondition: First team to repair 5 capes with correct sentences wins.

bossChallenges.scenario: A mysterious villain is testing new recruits with a counting challenge before letting them into the training hall.
bossChallenges.game: Number Gatekeeper: the villain (teacher) shows a number card and a hero must count their badges aloud correctly to pass.
bossChallenges.winCondition: The team that gets all members past the gatekeeper first enters the hall.

hooks: Quick warm-up: flash superhero greeting cards ('Hello!', 'Goodbye!') and students shout them back in a hero voice before the buzzer.
Play 'Secret Identity': the teacher whispers a hero name and students greet their partner as if meeting for the first time.
discoveries: Introduce a new hero puppet on the board. Model 'I am ___' with the puppet's name, then have students introduce themselves the same way.
Draw three heroes with different colored capes. Model 'He is...' / 'She is...' for each, then have students describe a hero of their choice.
conceptChecks: If I say 'She is fast,' am I talking about a boy or a girl hero?
Which word do we use for 'I' — am, is, or are?
sandboxActivities: In pairs, students take turns introducing themselves as a hero: 'Hello, I am ___!'
Students color a cape and describe it: 'My cape is ___.'

ruleRecaps: Recap: I + am, You/We/They + are, He/She/It + is. Blue box = the subject, Red box = the correct 'to be' word.
Board recap: 'He is a hero.' vs 'They are heroes.' — same idea, different subject.
matchingActivities: Drag-and-drop: match each subject pronoun (I, You, He, She) to its correct 'to be' word.
Students match a color card to a superhero item and say the full sentence out loud.
bossTasks: Each student introduces themselves as a hero with a full sentence: 'I am ___.'
Students interview a partner: 'What color is your cape?' and report back: 'His/Her cape is ___.'

bossChallenges.scenario: The lobby just opened and every player must call out their ready-check before the bus takes off.
bossChallenges.game: Ready-Check Relay: each player says 'I am ready!' or 'I am not ready!' before the timer hits zero, then passes to the next teammate.
bossChallenges.winCondition: First full squad to ready up with correct sentences drops first.

bossChallenges.scenario: A rival squad is trash-talking in chat and only correct grammar earns the right to clap back.
bossChallenges.game: Chat Clapback: teacher reads a trash-talk line, students respond with a correct 'He is / She is / They are' comeback sentence.
bossChallenges.winCondition: The squad with the cleanest comebacks wins the chat war.

bossChallenges.scenario: New skins just dropped in the shop and only correctly-formed sentences unlock them.
bossChallenges.game: Skin Shop Unlock: a skin card is revealed, students must say 'It is ___' with the color to claim it for their squad.
bossChallenges.winCondition: The squad that unlocks 5 skins first wins the shop.

hooks: Quick warm-up: flash gamer greeting cards ('Yo!', 'GG!') and students respond in character before the buzzer.
Play 'Ready Check': the teacher calls out a player name and students respond 'I am ready!' as fast as possible.
discoveries: Introduce a squad roster on the board with different players. Model 'He is...' / 'She is...' for each role, then have students describe a teammate.
Draw a lobby screen with ranks and skins. Model 'I am rank ___' and 'It is a ___ skin,' then have students create their own.
conceptChecks: If I say 'She is the sniper,' am I talking about a boy or a girl?
Which word goes with 'I' — am, is, or are?
sandboxActivities: In pairs, students introduce their gamer tag: 'Yo, I am ___!'
Students design a skin and describe it: 'It is ___.'

ruleRecaps: Recap: I + am, You/We/They + are, He/She/It + is. Blue = subject, Red = the correct 'to be' word.
Board recap: 'He is the sniper.' vs 'They are the squad.' — same idea, different subject.
matchingActivities: Drag-and-drop: match each subject pronoun to its correct 'to be' word on the lobby screen.
Students match a color card to a skin and say the full sentence.
bossTasks: Each student introduces their gamer tag with a full sentence: 'I am ___.'
Students interview a partner: 'What rank are you?' and report back: 'He/She is rank ___.'

bossChallenges.scenario: The Monster Nursery mixed up all the baby monsters! Trainers must claim the right pet before it wakes up hungry.
bossChallenges.game: Pet Claim Race: a monster card appears and a student must say 'This is my monster!' or point to a partner's monster saying 'That is his/her monster' correctly.
bossChallenges.winCondition: First team to correctly claim 5 monsters wins the nursery.

bossChallenges.scenario: A rival trainer is bragging about their family's monster collection at the Tamers' Fair.
bossChallenges.game: Family Brag Battle: students take turns describing a family member's pet: 'My brother's monster is ___' using possessives correctly.
bossChallenges.winCondition: The family with the most correct brags wins the fair.

bossChallenges.scenario: The Lost and Found box at Monster Camp is full of unclaimed toys and pets!
bossChallenges.game: Lost and Found Roleplay: a camper describes an item using 'his/her/my/your' and teammates must find the matching owner.
bossChallenges.winCondition: The team that returns all 5 items with correct grammar wins camp points.

hooks: Quick warm-up: flash family and pet picture cards, students race to name each one in English.
Play 'Whose Monster?': the teacher points to a drawn monster and asks 'Whose monster is this?' for students to guess.
discoveries: Draw a family tree of monster trainers on the board. Model 'This is my monster' / 'That is her monster' for each character, then have students describe their own.
Introduce a monster egg that hatches only when a student uses the right possessive to claim it.
conceptChecks: If I say 'her monster,' am I talking about a boy or a girl?
Which word do we use for something that belongs to me — my or your?
sandboxActivities: In pairs, students draw a pet monster and describe it: 'This is my monster. It is ___.'
Students interview a partner about their family: 'Is this your brother?' and answer with a full sentence.

ruleRecaps: Recap: my = mine, your = yours, his = a boy's, her = a girl's. Blue box = the owner, Red box = the possessive word.
Board recap: 'This is his monster.' vs 'This is her monster.' — same sentence, different owner.
matchingActivities: Drag-and-drop: match each possessive word to the correct family member or pet picture.
Students match a monster card to 'my/your/his/her' speech bubbles.
bossTasks: Each student describes their own pet or toy using 'my': 'This is my ___.'
Students interview a partner about their family's pet and report back: 'His/Her pet is a ___.'

bossChallenges.scenario: The Summon Gate opened and only trainers who claim their companion correctly can keep it!
bossChallenges.game: Summon Claim Race: a companion card appears and a student must say 'This is my companion!' correctly before the gate closes.
bossChallenges.winCondition: First team to claim 5 companions correctly wins the gate.

bossChallenges.scenario: Two rival guilds are comparing rosters before the big tournament.
bossChallenges.game: Roster Brag Battle: students describe a teammate's character using possessives: 'His character is ___' or 'Her weapon is ___.'
bossChallenges.winCondition: The guild with the most correct roster descriptions wins bragging rights.

bossChallenges.scenario: The Lost Inventory Vault is full of unclaimed gear after the server reset.
bossChallenges.game: Vault Roleplay: a player describes an item with 'his/her/my/your' and teammates find the matching owner.
bossChallenges.winCondition: The team that returns all 5 items with correct grammar wins the vault.

hooks: Quick warm-up: flash character and companion picture cards, students race to name each role in English.
Play 'Whose Loot?': the teacher shows a drawn item and asks 'Whose loot is this?' for students to guess.
discoveries: Draw a guild roster on the board. Model 'This is my companion' / 'That is her weapon' for each character, then have students describe their own.
Introduce a summon gate that only opens when a student uses the right possessive to claim their pull.
conceptChecks: If I say 'her weapon,' am I talking about a boy or a girl character?
Which word do we use for something that belongs to you — your or his?
sandboxActivities: In pairs, students draw their dream companion and describe it: 'This is my companion. It is ___.'
Students interview a partner about their guild: 'Is this your mentor?' and answer with a full sentence.

ruleRecaps: Recap: my = mine, your = yours, his = a boy character's, her = a girl character's. Blue = the owner, Red = the possessive word.
Board recap: 'This is his weapon.' vs 'This is her weapon.' — same sentence, different owner.
matchingActivities: Drag-and-drop: match each possessive word to the correct character or companion picture.
Students match a gear card to 'my/your/his/her' speech bubbles.
bossTasks: Each student describes their own favorite character using 'my': 'This is my ___.'
Students interview a partner about their guild's mentor and report back: 'His/Her mentor is a ___.'

bossChallenges.scenario: Training Day at the Monster Gym! Coaches must test each monster's abilities before the big tournament.
bossChallenges.game: Ability Test Relay: teacher calls an action, a student must say 'My monster can ___' or 'My monster can't ___' correctly and mime it.
bossChallenges.winCondition: First team to correctly test 5 abilities wins the training badge.

bossChallenges.scenario: The Whisper Challenge! Monsters must perform actions with the correct volume or the coach won't notice.
bossChallenges.game: Volume Roleplay: a student performs an action card while saying the adverb correctly, like 'I run quickly' or 'I speak quietly.'
bossChallenges.winCondition: The team with the most correct adverb sentences wins the challenge.

bossChallenges.scenario: It's the Gym Championship and only monsters with clearly pronounced 'can't' can enter the ring.
bossChallenges.game: Can/Can't Showdown: students must clearly pronounce the final 't' in 'can't' during a quickfire round, or the point doesn't count.
bossChallenges.winCondition: The team with the clearest pronunciation after 5 rounds wins the championship.

hooks: Quick warm-up: flash action verb cards (run, jump, swim) and students act them out before shouting the word.
Play 'Simon the Monster Says': students only do the action if the teacher says 'My monster can ___.'
discoveries: Draw a monster on the board and add abilities one by one. Model 'It can ___' / 'It can't ___' for each, then have students describe their own dream monster.
Introduce a training obstacle course. Model adverbs of manner like 'run quickly' and 'climb slowly' as students act each one out.
conceptChecks: If I say 'It can't fly,' does the monster have wings that work?
Which sound do we hear at the end of 'can't' that we don't hear in 'can'?
sandboxActivities: In pairs, students take turns saying what their monster can and can't do.
Students act out an action with the correct adverb while a partner guesses the word.

ruleRecaps: Recap: 'can' + verb for ability, 'can't' + verb for no ability. Blue box = can, Red box = can't — listen for that final 't' sound!
Board recap: adverbs of manner answer 'how' — run quickly, speak quietly, sing loudly.
matchingActivities: Drag-and-drop: match each action verb to 'can' or 'can't' based on the monster card shown.
Students match an action to its adverb (run → quickly, whisper → quietly).
bossTasks: Each student says one thing their monster can do and one thing it can't.
Students interview a partner: 'Can you swim?' and report back using the correct adverb of manner.

bossChallenges.game: Ability Check Relay: the commander (teacher) calls out an action, and a raider must say 'I can ___' or 'I can't ___' correctly before boarding.
bossChallenges.winCondition: First squad to correctly confirm 5 abilities boards the chopper and wins.

bossChallenges.scenario: Stealth Mission Alert! Any noise above the limit blows the raiders' cover.
bossChallenges.game: Stealth Roleplay: students perform an action while saying the correct adverb, like 'I move quietly' or 'I sprint quickly.'

bossChallenges.game: Radio Check Showdown: students must clearly pronounce the final 't' in 'can't' during a rapid-fire radio drill.
bossChallenges.winCondition: The team with the clearest pronunciation after 5 rounds gets resupplied first.

hooks: Quick warm-up: flash raider ability cards (hack, snipe, sprint) and students act them out before shouting the word.
Play 'Commander Says': students only act if the teacher says 'You can ___.'
discoveries: Draw a raider loadout on the board and add abilities one by one. Model 'She can ___' / 'She can't ___' for each, then have students build their own raider.
Introduce an obstacle course extraction map. Model adverbs of manner like 'sprint quickly' and 'hack quietly' as students act each one out.
conceptChecks: If I say 'He can't fly,' does the raider have a jetpack that works?
Which sound do we hear at the end of 'can't' that we don't hear in 'can'?
sandboxActivities: In pairs, students take turns saying what their raider can and can't do.
Students act out an action with the correct adverb while a partner guesses it.

ruleRecaps: Recap: 'can' + verb for ability, 'can't' + verb for no ability. Blue = can, Red = can't — listen for that final 't' sound!
Board recap: adverbs of manner answer 'how' — sprint quickly, hack quietly, move carefully.
matchingActivities: Drag-and-drop: match each ability to 'can' or 'can't' based on the raider card shown.
Students match an action to its adverb (sprint → quickly, sneak → quietly).
bossTasks: Each student says one thing their raider can do and one thing they can't.
Students interview a partner: 'Can you hack?' and report back using the correct adverb of manner.

bossChallenges.scenario: A tricky villain only gets defeated by heroes who use perfect grammar in their battle cries!

hooks: Quick warm-up: show hero photo cards and students describe the action using 'He/She' before the buzzer.
Play 'Guess the Hero': the teacher describes a hero in third person and students guess who it is.
discoveries: Draw two heroes on the board, one boy one girl. Model 'He plays...' and 'She reads...' for daily habits, adding the -s each time with emphasis.
Introduce a mystery classmate description game — model third person sentences and have students guess who's being described.

sandboxActivities: In pairs, students describe a partner's daily habit using 'He/She ___s.'
Students draw a hero and write three -s sentences about their routine.

Board recap: 'I play' vs 'He plays' — same verb, different ending for third person.
matchingActivities: Drag-and-drop: match the base verb to its correct -s form for he/she sentences.
Students match a hero action card to the correct pronoun (He/She) and say the full sentence.
bossTasks: Each student describes a classmate's habit with a correct -s sentence.
Students interview a partner about their weekend and report back in third person.

matchingActivities: Drag-and-drop: match each opinion to its correct reason using 'because.'
Students match an opinion statement to 'agree' or 'disagree' based on their own view.
bossTasks: Each student shares one opinion about a streamer with a reason.
Students interview a partner about their opinion and report back using 'He/She thinks that ___.'

gapFills: 1. ________ (First/Finally), we chopped the vegetables for the ramen.
2. ________ (Then/First), we boiled the water for the noodles.
3. ________ (After that/First), we added the special sauce.
4. ________ (Finally/Then), the judges tasted every bowl.
5. First, we ________ (cook/cooked) the noodles for ten minutes.
6. Then, the chef ________ (add/added) the secret spices.
7. After that, we ________ (serve/served) the ramen to the judges.
8. Finally, our team ________ (win/won) first place!
9. First we cooked, ________ (then/finally) we cleaned the kitchen.
10. ________ (First/After that), we are going to enter next year's contest too.

bossChallenges.scenario: Story Time at the Ramen Festival! Chefs must retell the whole cook-off from start to finish.
bossChallenges.game: Full Story Relay: each teammate adds one part of the story using First/Then/After that/Finally in the correct order.
bossChallenges.winCondition: First team to tell the complete story in order wins the storyteller trophy.

bossChallenges.scenario: The Judges' Panel wants a perfectly organized report of how the winning dish was made.
bossChallenges.game: Recipe Report: students present their cooking steps in order using connectors and correct past tense.
bossChallenges.winCondition: The team with the clearest, most complete report wins Best Presentation.

bossChallenges.scenario: A mixed-up storybook has all the cook-off events out of order and needs fixing before the festival ends!
bossChallenges.game: Story Order Showdown: teams receive scrambled event cards and must arrange and retell them using First/Then/After that/Finally.
bossChallenges.winCondition: The team that reorders and retells the story first with zero mistakes wins the festival prize.

conceptChecks: Which connector do we use to start a story — First, Then, or Finally?
Do connectors go at the beginning or the end of a sentence?
sandboxActivities: In pairs, students tell a partner their own cook-off story using all four connectors.
Students draw a four-panel comic of an adventure and label each panel with a connector.
